title: Firstborn of All Creation
speaker: Jonathan Baird
summary: Firstborn was a title of inheritance, not just birth order. David, the youngest son, was called firstborn. Jesus is heir of all creation.
exhortation: Today we're putting a magnifying glass on one phrase: Jesus is "the firstborn of all creation." That phrase could easily trip us up. What does it mean? Was Jesus created, as many cults believe? Was he the first thing made?

Look at what firstborn meant in the Bible. It had a very specific role in the ancient world. The firstborn had particular rights and carried on the wealth, name and reputation of the family. The firstborn received the inheritance. But curiously, the firstborn wasn't always the first one born. It was a title and a role, not just birth order. Often the first son held it, but sometimes he lost it, and there are places in the Bible where the term is used of someone who wasn't born first.

One in particular is Psalm 89:27: "And I will make him the firstborn, the highest of the kings of the earth." That is speaking of King David, who was actually the youngest son in his family. That can't be an accident. David, the man after God's own heart, from whom Jesus descended, was the last and youngest, and yet he is called the firstborn. He had the anointing. He was the heir who would carry on the line, and the whole kingdom belonged to him.

So Jesus, the promised Messiah from David's line, is not only the firstborn of the kingdoms of the earth and the heir of the promises to David. He is the firstborn of all creation itself. All creation is his inheritance. He owns it all and has dominion over all things, and he is worthy of our praise.
prayer: Lord, I pray for those who are struggling with sin today and feeling the weight of guilt. Bring us to you, who paid the price for every sin with your own blood and defeated it on the cross, not so that we can wallow in it, but so that we can bring it to you, repent and be forgiven.

I pray for those who are racked with fear about the day, whose anxiety is starting to crush their hope and take over their minds. Meet them. Help them trust you with all their heart and not lean on their own understanding, and acknowledge you in all their ways, and you will make their paths straight. Fill them with hope and even joy today that you reign over all things and are with us every step of the way. Thank you that we can come to you, Jesus, because you first came to us. In Jesus' name, amen.
